newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-RATHORE CENTURY BOOSTS INDIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-RATHORE CENTURY BOOSTS INDIA.

text.p: Vikram Rathore scored a fine century as India moved to 24 runs short of Free State's first innings score before declaring at 296 for six at Springbok Park on Sunday.
The 27-year-old Rathore held the innings together with 115 from 203 balls after India resumed at 56 for one on the second day of the three-day match.
He hit 16 fours and reached his century with the second of three sixes. The impressive knock may have propelled Rathore into the side for the third test ahead of fellow opener Workeri Raman.
But when Rathore was caught at first slip just before tea India were again in trouble at 198 for six. They were rescued by an unbroken stand of 98 between V.V.S. Laxman and wicketkeeper Saba Karim.
Karim was the more aggressive of the two, making 53 from 98 balls with nine boundaries, but Laxman did his own confidence no harm ahead of the test with a composed 56 from 125 balls with eight fours.
When acting captain Anil Kumble called the innings to a halt, Free State were left with 18 overs to face before the close.
Deon Jordaan (33) and Gerhardus Liebenberg (30) set up the possibility of an exciting finish on the final day with an unbroken first wicket stand of 69.
Free State, who made 320 for seven declared in their first innings, lead by 93 runs and will look to score quickly on the final morning to set up a declaration soon after lunch.
